items.q: What should you remember about **Productive ≠ profitable**?
items.a: **Claude is tuned for** agreement and completion feelings, not business outcomes.

items.q: What should you remember about **AI sycophancy is measured**?
items.a: **"Elephant" study**: models fail to push back on framing ~88% of the time (humans ~60%); personalization/memory makes it worse.

items.q: What should you remember about **Council beats single-perspective advice**?
items.a: **side-by-side demo**: plain Claude gave generic "rework it" feedback; roast council gave scored personas, CAC/LTV analysis, and a concrete 48-hour test.

items.q: What should you remember about **Verification is a habit, not one button**?
items.a: **define "done" per domain; build** loop (create → verify → fix → repeat); then adversarial stress testing.

items.q: What should you remember about **First shot ~65%, verification gets ~90%**?
items.a: **same benchmark Cole Medin** cites; less human rework on review.

items.q: What should you remember about **Context rot starts early**?
items.a: **longer conversations make Claude** dumber even on simple tasks; more context is not better.

items.q: What should you remember about **Session handoff > compact**?
items.a: **Nate finds /compact slow; custom handoff** skill preserves state across /clear and enables cross-tool transfer (e.g. to Codex).

items.q: What should you remember about **Parallel sub-agents for independent work**?
items.a: **each gets a clean context window; synthesize after.**

items.q: What should you remember about **/goal separates worker from judge**?
items.a: **addresses the same sycophancy** problem at completion time; objective done-criteria work best.

items.q: What should you remember about **Role shift: builder → reviewer**?
items.a: **with all four upgrades,** human becomes problem-solver, decision-maker, and judge.
